newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran welcomes Arab League decisions on Israel ties.
newsitem.headline: Iran welcomes Arab League decisions on Israel ties.

text.p: Iran on Wednesday welcomed Arab League resolutions recommending Arab states freeze the normalisation of ties with Israel, but expressed regret over the backing given to the United Arab Emirates in a territorial dispute with Tehran.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi, quoted by Tehran radio, said: "The Islamic Republic of Iran, as flag-bearer of the front for the liberation of sacred Qods (Jerusalem) and for the defence of the Palestinian nation's rights, welcomes any measure aimed at realising these aims."
Arab foreign ministers recommended on Monday after a two-day meeting in Cairo that Arab states put an end to normal ties with Israel and restore the old economic boycott of the Jewish state.
The ministers also recommended closing down Israeli missions and withdrawing from multilateral talks on Middle East peace.
Non-Arab Iran has no ties with Israel which it says has no right to exist. Tehran opposes the Middle East peace process which it condemns as a sellout of the Palestinians' rights.
Mohammadi also expressed regret over the Cairo meeting's support for the UAE in its dispute with Iran over three Gulf islands.

He repeated Tehran's stance that the islands of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs were an "inseparable part of Iran's territory" and that it was ready for talks with the UAE to clear up any "misunderstandings".
